exposure: experience of recent delivery (facility vs. home, post-delivery health problems, pain relief, cost)
perceived benefits (availability of medicine, health benefits for mother and baby, good care)
outcome: women's experience of delivery care during home and facility births
women's preference for future delivery site (facility-based or home)
cohort: The study included 500 recently delivered women (210 delivered at a facility and 290 delivered at home) from a district of Jharkhand state in India.
finding: Women with higher education, above 25 years, who currently delivered at a facility, and had health problems post-delivery were significant predictors of future facility-based delivery, with availability of medicines and perceived health benefits being key reasons for preference.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women recently after their delivery.
